name: Asset Management & Private Equity
one_liner: Asset managers and private equity firms invest other people's money for fees and performance-based carry, so their economics hinge on assets under management and the fee rate per dollar.
how_it_makes_money: Traditional asset managers charge a management fee as a percentage of assets under management, with passive funds far cheaper than active. Private equity and other alternatives typically charge a management fee on committed capital (classically ~2%) plus carried interest (classically ~20% of profits above a hurdle), and some earn transaction and monitoring fees.
revenue_formula: Management fees = AUM (or committed capital) × fee rate, where AUM change = net flows + market performance
Carried interest = (exit proceeds - invested capital - hurdle) × carry %
LBO equity return = EBITDA growth + multiple expansion + debt paydown
cost_structure: Compensation: investment professionals' salaries, bonuses and carry, the dominant cost
Distribution: fees to platforms, advisors and placement agents
Technology and data: trading systems, research data, risk tools
Fund and operating expenses: legal, compliance, fund administration
In LBOs, interest on acquisition debt is borne by the portfolio company
margins: Scaled asset managers often earn operating margins of roughly 30-40%, with passive giants relying on volume and active managers under fee pressure; PE firms' fee-related earnings are steady while carry is lumpy and tied to exits.

key_metrics.name: Assets under management (AUM)
key_metrics.what: Total assets managed; the base on which fees are charged.

key_metrics.name: Net flows
key_metrics.what: New money in minus redemptions; the clearest sign of client demand.

key_metrics.name: Fee rate (bps)
key_metrics.what: Revenue per dollar of AUM; captures product mix and pricing power.

key_metrics.name: Internal rate of return (IRR)
key_metrics.what: Annualized return on a fund's cash flows; the headline PE performance measure.

key_metrics.name: Multiple on invested capital (MOIC / TVPI)
key_metrics.what: Total value returned relative to capital invested; complements IRR.

key_metrics.name: Dry powder
key_metrics.what: Committed but uninvested capital; signals deployment pressure and future fees.

key_metrics.name: Fee-related earnings (FRE)
key_metrics.what: Profit from recurring management fees, valued more highly than volatile carry.

trends: Continued shift from active to passive and ETF products, compressing fees
Private credit growing rapidly as alternatives managers lend in place of banks
Alternatives firms targeting wealthy individuals and retirement savings
Slow exit markets leading to continuation funds and pressure on distributions
Industry consolidation as managers seek scale and multi-asset breadth
Higher financing costs shifting PE value creation toward operational improvement
